components.name: measurement
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: one line -> statistical error from the goodness of the profile fit; chi2-curvature sigma of this line, rescaled to red_chi2 = 1

evidence.likelihood: synthesis chi2 over the fit window, curvature at the best abundance
evidence.correlation_treatment: red_chi2 rescaling absorbs pixel correlation and model inadequacy; the worse-constrained side is taken

components.name: transition_data
components.source: gf covariance per data/reference/gf_error_model.csv -- AL_AGSS21: fully_correlated (scale 0.0000 dex; Nordlander & Lind 2017 A&A 607 A75 Table A.1 + Sect. 2.1.2; Burheim, Hartman & Nilsson 2023 A&A 672 A197 Table 3)

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: stellar.xi
components.source: per-line paired differential at xi 0.90/1.10 on this product's OWN pool, stamped legs (RYA-1178 A)

evidence.response_assessment: central paired median over 1 lines; difference of aggregates 0.0150/km/s

components.name: continuum
components.source: standing continuum rule (synthesis reference, 3-MAD clipped): placement = q97 vs q80 central half-difference, REFERENCE = IAG-atlas leg minus nominal, in quadrature, paired on this pool

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: fit window +/-0.25 A core vs the band's fixed window, paired on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: MARCS.GES vs ATLAS9.Castelli, one axis varied, paired on this pool

components.name: telluric
components.source: per-line measured sky depth -> measured residual of this holding vs an independent correction on the telluric pixels -> dex via the line's own dA/df (+0.1% leg); lines independent, weight 1/n

per_line.residual_basis: solar_crires_plus_y_wide_rya1054 vs independent correction solar_kpno_molecfit_corrected, baseline-removed

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

evidence.owed_measurement: a paired molecule-strength leg on this C/O pool

components.name: nlte
components.source: this leg applies no departures (nlte_delta_dex = 0 on every line)

components.name: pseudo_continuum
components.source: outside the near-UV the continuum is observed; it is placed per line by the standing rule and priced on `continuum`

components.name: hfs_isotopes
components.source: optically thin limit: every hyperfine-split pool line is <= 0.1 deep (catalogued), so its EW is the total gf regardless of the splitting; the components are in the synthesis list (VALD lab HFS)

components.name: molecular_coupling
components.source: atomic product; the selector is not a MOL- indicator set

components.name: holding_instrument
components.source: SynthesisHandler harness residual MEASURED against the known optical answer (RYA-869)

uncertainty.covariance_source: components independent of one another; the shared-source gf correlation lives inside transition_data
uncertainty.assumptions: solar log g and [Fe/H] pinned; Teff allowance 1 K

products.sigma_asplund_basis: Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021 Sect. 2.1: statistical (+) half the 3D effect (+) NLTE (half the correction, floor 0.03); molecules: Amarsi+2021 compositional term instead of NLTE, trend term not priced; atomic data and observational terms not included
products.stat_basis_declared: quantiser-floor 0.01 dex (RYA-771) — UNMEASURED: line-to-line scatter at n_lines=1; the floor STANDS IN for a scatter that was never determined, it is not a measurement of one

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). Reported LTE. nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1213: the two new near-UV Fe I Reference Gerber-LTE rows landed after the previous annotation pass. Every near-UV product must state the band's residual opacity deficit or it reads as a converged answer.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

products.line_set_basis: DERIVED at read time from `tier` by pipeline.reference_lineset.line_set_for_product -- not stored as an identity field (RYA-1127). Shown here for readability; the identity key resolves it independently.
products.xi_note: pool of 2 lines is below min_paired=3: no xi derivative is published (RYA-1224)
products.sigma_reported_basis: quadrature(sigma_stat, sigma_syst_complete) where sigma_syst_complete = quadrature(published sigma_syst, sigma_xi). sigma_xi enters ONCE, through sigma_syst_complete — the RYA-1120 artifact's own sigma_reported omitted sigma_syst altogether.
products.sigma_reported_caveat: INCOMPLETE: no dA/dxi exists for this pool, so the xi term is absent from this bar rather than zero. The bar is a LOWER BOUND.

irreducible_dispersion.basis: sigma_stat x sqrt(n_lines); valid because sigma_stat is the STANDARD ERROR of the mean — verified against the per-line layer on the VIS products that carry both (std/sqrt(n) reproduces the published stat_dex; the raw std does not)
irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

products.sigma_reported_basis: quadrature(sigma_stat, sigma_syst_complete) where sigma_syst_complete = quadrature(published sigma_syst, sigma_xi). sigma_xi enters ONCE, through sigma_syst_complete — the RYA-1120 artifact's own sigma_reported omitted sigma_syst altogether.
products.aggregate_collision_note: Published A is the MEDIAN of the per-line abundances (nlte_effect.json: aggregator=median). LTE 7.541 / NLTE 7.562 — the <3D>-NLTE departure is live and separates the pair on this holding.

irreducible_dispersion.basis: sigma_stat x sqrt(n_lines); valid because sigma_stat is the STANDARD ERROR of the mean — verified against the per-line layer on the VIS products that carry both (std/sqrt(n) reproduces the published stat_dex; the raw std does not)
irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

products.sigma_reported_basis: quadrature(sigma_stat, sigma_syst_complete) where sigma_syst_complete = quadrature(published sigma_syst, sigma_xi). sigma_xi enters ONCE, through sigma_syst_complete — the RYA-1120 artifact's own sigma_reported omitted sigma_syst altogether.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). products.xi_note: full 3D resolves the velocity field xi stands in for, so the PUBLISHED value carries no net xi dependence: it is a sum A(1D-LTE)(xi) + aberr(xi) whose two halves move oppositely. Recorded, not silent — the Amarsi MLP DOES take vmic as an input axis and its correction moves d(aberr)/dxi = +0.0985 dex/(km/s); the exemption is about the sum, not the call (Ryan, 2026-08-29). This product is ALSO a reference-set replication anchor, not a xi-varying measurement of ours — N/A on either ground (RYA-1185).

products.aggregate_collision_note: Published A is the MEDIAN of the per-line abundances (nlte_effect.json: aggregator=median). On this holding the <3D>-LTE and <3D>-NLTE medians coincide at 7.552 while their MEANS differ by +0.0267 dex and the NLTE departure moves 66 of 67 lines. The pair is NOT byte-identical and the NLTE leg is NOT unwired: the same code path on kpno_kurucz2005 gives 7.541 vs 7.562. Genuine median coincidence, kept as two products (RYA-1178 Part 0).

products.xi_note: full 3D resolves the velocity field xi stands in for, so the PUBLISHED value carries no net xi dependence: it is a sum A(1D-LTE)(xi) + aberr(xi) whose two halves move oppositely. Recorded, not silent — the Amarsi MLP DOES take vmic as an input axis and its correction moves d(aberr)/dxi = +0.0985 dex/(km/s); the exemption is about the sum, not the call (Ryan, 2026-08-29).

products.aggregate_collision_note: Published A is the MEDIAN of the per-line abundances (nlte_effect.json: aggregator=median). On this holding the <3D>-LTE and <3D>-NLTE medians coincide at 7.552 while their MEANS differ by +0.0267 dex and the NLTE departure moves 66 of 67 lines. The pair is NOT byte-identical and the NLTE leg is NOT unwired: the same code path on kpno_kurucz2005 gives 7.541 vs 7.562. Genuine median coincidence, kept as two products (RYA-1178 Part 0).

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1213: the two new near-UV Fe I Reference Gerber-LTE rows landed after the previous annotation pass. Every near-UV product must state the band's residual opacity deficit or it reads as a converged answer.

components.name: transition_data

components.name: stellar.teff

components.name: continuum
components.source: standing continuum rule (synthesis reference, 3-MAD clipped): placement = q97 vs q80 central half-difference, REFERENCE = IAG-atlas leg minus nominal, in quadrature, paired on this pool

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: fit window +/-0.25 A core vs the band's fixed window, paired on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: MARCS.GES vs ATLAS9.Castelli, one axis varied, paired on this pool

components.name: telluric

products.aggregate_collision_note: Published A is the MEDIAN of the per-line abundances (nlte_effect.json: aggregator=median). On this holding the <3D>-LTE and <3D>-NLTE medians coincide at 7.552 while their MEANS differ by +0.0267 dex and the NLTE departure moves 66 of 67 lines. components.source: per-feature scatter of the accepted pool (components within 0.5 A merged, RYA-1232)

components.name: transition_data

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: stellar.xi
components.source: per-line paired differential at xi 0.90/1.10 on this product's OWN pool, stamped legs (RYA-1178 A)

evidence.response_assessment: central paired median over 2 lines; difference of aggregates -0.0025/km/s

components.name: continuum
components.source: standing continuum rule (synthesis reference, 3-MAD clipped): placement = q97 vs q80 central half-difference, REFERENCE = IAG-atlas leg minus nominal, in quadrature, paired on this pool

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: fit window +/-0.25 A core vs the band's fixed window, paired on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: MARCS.GES vs ATLAS9.Castelli, one axis varied, paired on this pool

components.name: telluric
components.source: per-line measured sky depth -> measured residual of this holding vs an independent correction on the telluric pixels -> dex via the line's own dA/df (+0.1% leg); lines independent, weight 1/n

per_line.residual_basis: solar_iag vs independent correction solar_kpno_kurucz2005_corrected, baseline-removed

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

evidence.owed_measurement: a paired molecule-strength leg on this C/O pool

components.name: nlte
components.source: this leg applies no departures (nlte_delta_dex = 0 on every line)

components.name: pseudo_continuum
components.source: outside the near-UV the continuum is observed; it is placed per line by the standing rule and priced on `continuum`

components.name: hfs_isotopes
components.source: every pool line has hfs_n_components == 1 (canonical_gf)

components.name: molecular_coupling
components.source: atomic product; the selector is not a MOL- indicator set

components.name: holding_instrument
components.source: SynthesisHandler harness residual MEASURED against the known optical answer (RYA-869)

uncertainty.covariance_source: components independent of one another; the shared-source gf correlation lives inside transition_data
uncertainty.assumptions: solar log g and [Fe/H] pinned; Teff allowance 1 K

components.name: continuum
components.source: standing continuum rule (synthesis reference, 3-MAD clipped): placement = q97 vs q80 central half-difference, REFERENCE = IAG-atlas leg minus nominal, in quadrature, paired on this pool

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: fit window +/-0.25 A core vs the band's fixed window, paired on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: MARCS.GES vs ATLAS9.Castelli, one axis varied, paired on this pool

components.name: telluric
components.source: per-line measured sky depth -> measured residual of this holding vs an independent correction on the telluric pixels -> dex via the line's own dA/df (+0.1% leg); lines independent, weight 1/n

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

components.name: pseudo_continuum

components.name: hfs_isotopes

components.name: molecular_coupling

components.name: holding_instrument

uncertainty.covariance_source: components independent of one another; the shared-source gf correlation lives inside transition_data

telluric.note: no admissible fit; band NOT corrected

DETERMINE-AND-GATE (RYA-460): the optical is telluric-light, so the owed action is a red-edge disposition, NOT a molecfit run. Any line inside 6867-6884 A needs exclusion or correction; lines blueward of it are CLEAN_OUTSIDE_REGISTERED_BANDS.

blockers.why: ESO ships a GDAS tarball for PARANAL ONLY, so a per-night La Silla profile had to be pulled by hand. RYA-983 automated the NOAA ARL archive (byte-range, 10.7 MB per night rather than 599 MB), so this is unblocked but not yet run.

the NOAA ARL GDAS1 archive begins there. Under the RYA-380 no-standard-atmosphere rule those frames can never be corrected by this route — a PERMANENT gap, not a backlog item. Three of tau Ceti's 32 HARPS nights sit below it.

measure_band_ew._INSTRUMENT_HOLDINGS still contains no non-solar holding and HoldingSpec carries no star, so there is nothing to point the harness at. RYA-985 made the synthesis star-generic; the holding half is open.

caveats.note: Y/J/H close within 1.93 km/s on every frame; K2148 and K2192 rail on tau Ceti and K2148 failed on alpha Cen. The CORRECTION is unaffected (the fit is topocentric and never uses the zero-point) but an absolute RV from a K frame is not trustworthy.
rests on the acen_orbit branch assignment RYA-963 left CONTESTED: the CRIRES pair says it is inverted, RYA-384's NIRPS anchor says it is not, and both cannot be right.

components.name: stellar.logg
components.source: solar log g is pinned; delta_logg is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.metallicity
components.source: solar [Fe/H] is pinned; delta_feh is definitionally zero (RYA-1089)

components.name: stellar.teff
components.source: sourced DEFINED zero (RYA-1226 convention): the solar Teff allowance is 1 K

evidence.owed_measurement: a Teff perturbation on this pool

components.name: stellar.xi
components.source: per-line paired differential at xi 0.90/1.10 on this product's OWN pool, stamped legs (RYA-1178 A)

evidence.response_assessment: central paired median over 3 lines; difference of aggregates -0.0125/km/s

components.name: continuum
components.source: standing continuum rule (synthesis reference, 3-MAD clipped): placement = q97 vs q80 central half-difference, REFERENCE = IAG-atlas leg minus nominal, in quadrature, paired on this pool

components.name: profile_ew
components.source: fit window +/-0.25 A core vs the band's fixed window, paired on this pool

components.name: model_atmosphere
components.source: MARCS.GES vs ATLAS9.Castelli, one axis varied, paired on this pool

components.name: telluric
components.source: per-line measured sky depth -> measured residual of this holding vs an independent correction on the telluric pixels -> dex via the line's own dA/df (+0.1% leg); lines independent, weight 1/n

components.name: blends
components.source: full atomic + molecular synthesis in-window (RYA-1230 turned molecular opacity on in every band); no catalogued-blend deficit

evidence.owed_measurement: a paired molecule-strength leg on this C/O pool

components.name: nlte
components.source: Asplund+2021 Sect. 2.1: half the non-LTE abundance correction, minimum 0.03 dex -- the correction measured on this pool (median 1D-NLTE delta of the accepted lines)

components.name: pseudo_continuum
components.source: outside the near-UV the continuum is observed; it is placed per line by the standing rule and priced on `continuum`

components.name: hfs_isotopes
components.source: every pool line has hfs_n_components == 1 (canonical_gf)

components.name: molecular_coupling
components.source: atomic product; the selector is not a MOL- indicator set

components.name: holding_instrument
components.source: SynthesisHandler harness residual MEASURED against the known optical answer (RYA-869)

uncertainty.covariance_source: components independent of one another; the shared-source gf correlation lives inside transition_data
uncertainty.assumptions: solar log g and [Fe/H] pinned; Teff allowance 1 K

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

RYA-1133 measured the two Kitt Peak holdings returning 7.957 vs 7.697 on the SAME 12 lines - 0.260 dex apart, half-spread 0.130 - so the run's term is breached by its own holdings and 0.130 is published instead. nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

products_withheld.opacity_note: RYA-1190: the near-UV continuum offset is BLEND-DRIVEN, not a continuum error -- 59 lines/A, 0 of 10 clean side-bands, and no isolated Fe I line exists in the band (minimum neighbour depth 0.790). Our near-UV list IS already the full VALD extract (0 of 62,072 rows missing), so completing the line list cannot close it; a deeper re-extraction is worth <=0.028 dex. REPORTED AND NOTED, NOT ADOPTED: the solar Fe headline rests on the VIS anchor 7.466, not on these rows.
products_withheld.annotation_reason: RYA-1203 item 3: record the RYA-1190 near-UV opacity-deficit limit
products_withheld.superseded_reason: RYA-1207: near-UV synthesis now includes molecular opacity (OH A-X, NH, CH, CN violet) — real solar near-UV absorbers the band carried NONE of, because every molecular list iSpec ships starts at 400 nm. Physics, not a fit: nothing calibrated to a target (RYA-161). Paired against a molecules-off run on this same code, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.28..-0.33 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and 4 windows containing no molecular line bit-identical.

nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. products_withheld.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

products_withheld.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.

irreducible_dispersion.reducible_by: PARTLY laboratory gf for NIR Fe I; a LARGE PART was non-convergent fits and has already been removed (RYA-1191)
irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

irreducible_dispersion.note: 🔴 RYA-1191 RE-DERIVED THIS NOTE AND MOST OF IT WAS FALSE. It read 'gf-limited dispersion, IRREDUCIBLE under the current NIR line list ... KP ENGINE-A 1.315 at n=7 is the exception that proves it — CRIRES+ curated lab-gf is ~6x tighter at n=5'. That 1.315 is ONE NON-CONVERGENT FIT: line 9437.793 returned A = 10.988 on this holding and 4.539 on solar_iag — same line, same gf, 6.4 dex apart, red_chi2 246 and 152, with excluded_reason blank on both because constraint_gate asks only whether a fit was CONSTRAINED and its frac_rise_weaker is NaN. Rejected by pipeline.fit_validity, the dispersion is 0.144 at n=6 — not an exception, and INDISTINGUISHABLE from CRIRES+'s 0.138. The ~6x ratio was that one line. ⚠️ NOTE ALSO that solar_iag NIR ENGINE-A already read 0.177 here because its committed product had excluded the same line; the 7x gap between the two holdings was an exclusion difference, not a telluric one. WHAT SURVIVES, re-measured on guarded pools: the NIR many-line bars are still the widest (IAG 0.307 at n=22, KP 0.386 at n=23) against the few-line curated ones (CRIRES+ 0.138 at n=5, KP ENGINE-A 0.144 at n=6), so the dispersion still tracks gf QUALITY rather than line count and adding VALD3-grade NIR lines would still widen it. But it is NOT IRREDUCIBLE: it more than HALVED when non-convergent fits were removed (KP 1D-LTE 0.895 -> 0.386, IAG 1D-LTE 0.949 -> 0.307). ⚠️ dispersion_dex above is the PRE-GUARD value and is regenerated when the product is. Report-and-note per RYA-777.

products_withheld.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products_withheld.annotation_reason: RYA-1208: the two near-UV Fe II `synth-1D-LTE-gerber` cells carry the band's opacity state like every other near-UV product. They were run on the post-RYA-1207 code, so molecular opacity IS included -- verified against the pool rather than assumed: this leg reads 7.422 beside its molecules-on 1D-LTE sibling at 7.402 on the same 12-line pool, where a molecules-OFF run would sit ~0.3 dex higher (RYA-1207 measured the Fe II lever at -0.276..-0.332 dex). The note is the band's, copied verbatim so every near-UV product states the same residual.
